content:
maria: quick proposal for packaging quant profiles that Redwood Optimize will recommend — want quick sanity check
ajay: drop it here, happy to weigh in. goal: make profiles discoverable + safe to auto-apply, right? :+1:
sophia: yes, and pluggable across AWQ/GPTQ/INT8/FP8 variants. also need accuracy delta metadata for rollout decisions
maria: exactly. rough sketch: single tarball with a manifest.json that lists model-arch, quant-backend, quant-params, eval-metrics (delta vs fp16), deploy-hints (batching, cache-friendly), and a compatibility hash for runtime kernel selection
oliver: example manifest snippet?
maria: sure — short example:
```json
{
  "name": "redwood/llama-3-13b",
  "version": "v1.2",
  "quant_backend": "awq",
  "quant_params": "4bit_groupwise,block_size=128",
  "eval_metrics": {"mmlu_delta": -1.2, "pppl_delta": 0.4},
  "deploy_hints": {"min_batch_delay_ms": 8, "kv_cache_mode": "shared"},
  "compat_hash": "sha256:abcd..."
}
```
ajay: looks good. suggest adding a `safety_profile` key to indicate when fallback to higher precision is recommended (e.g., critical prompts where delta > X)
sophia: also suggest `preferred_runtime_versions` array so Optimize can avoid runtimes with known regression for that profile
maria: good call. another operational thing: file naming and versioning. propose `qpkg-{model}-{backend}-{version}.tar.gz`, e.g. `qpkg-llama3-13b-awq-v1.2.tar.gz`. inside manifest `version` is authoritative
oliver: +1. how do we handle multiple candidate quantizations from a bakeoff? e.g., awq-int4 vs gptq-int4 with slightly different deltas and perf
maria: treat each candidate as its own package with semantic versioning and `eval_metadata/bakeoff_id` linking them to the same experiment group. Optimize UI can present them as alternatives with tradeoff sliders
ml-eval-bot: bakeoff 2028-02-12: group_id bg-542, candidates: qpkg-llama3-13b-awq-v1.2 (latency -22%, mmlu_delta -1.2), qpkg-llama3-13b-gptq-v0.9 (latency -18%, mmlu_delta -0.7)
ajay: nice bot summary. for rollout policy we need: "apply_thresholds": {"max_mmlu_delta": 1.5, "max_pppl_delta": 1.0}, and an auto-rollback window with metrics baseline
sophia: and schema for `eval_datasets` — list of named evals + sample sizes + seed so others can reproduce deltas
maria: agree. I'll update the doc with keys: name, version, quant_backend, quant_params, eval_metrics (per dataset), bakeoff_link, bakeoff_id, deploy_hints, preferred_runtime_versions, safety_profile, compat_hash, apply_thresholds
oliver: one more: `storage_size_bytes` to help cost estimate in Optimize when recommending between profiles
maria: love that. final note on naming: we'll reserve `qpkg-` prefix for Optimize-published profiles. internal experiments can use `qexp-` prefix. that keeps discovery sane
ajay: can you add a short CLI for packing/unpacking and manifest validation? small script to fail when eval metrics missing
maria: yes, draft a validator that enforces required keys and checks semantic versioning. I'll post a PR today. thanks all :raised_hands:
ml-eval-bot: pushed bakeoff summary to /s3/redwood/quant-bakeoffs/bg-542/manifest.json
maria: cool — next steps: PR for manifest schema + naming guidelines, and a short Optimize UI story to surface alternatives. tagging this thread for implementation planning
